findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following foods stored without covering:

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)  
At approximately 11:15am, the facility had cheese sauce and house made marinara on the hot well at 109F and 85F respectively. The foods were not ready to serve. The facility opens for service at 11am. The items had been in the hot holding unit for less than an hour. Temperature on hot well unit was turned up. The house marinara came up to 165F on it’s own in the hot well  before it was served.  The cheese sauce was removed from the hot holding well and placed on a double boiler to bring the cheese sauce up to 165F. Highly suggest reheating on the stove top before placing food in the hot holding well for service.

(D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed improper thawing of ground beef. Ground beef was in a basin of cold water thawing. Cease practice. Thawing should occur in refrigeration under 41 degrees F or completely submerged in running water and not having a temperature above 41 degrees F. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated an employee had done this before lunch rush. Discuss proper thawing techniques with staff. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 & 2-301.14 Cook had a wiping cloth hanging from his back pocket. When asked about the use of said cloth, cook noted he uses it to wipe his hands. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage upon request of inspector. Cook was advised if hands need to be wiped then they should be properly washed at a designated handsink, and disposable paper towels need to be used to wipe hands upon completing handwashing. 
Cook handled his a cell phone and then prepared to put on gloves without first washing hands. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. 
Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. The process took less than 20 seconds, and a barrier was not used to shut off the manual faucet. Cook was advised on proper handwashing. Proper handwashing technique poster was observed at the kitchen handsink. 

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.  To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Food employee stated cheese sauce in a stock pot was cooked 2 hours prior to inspection, cheese sauce was found cooling in stock pot located in the walk-in cooler and measured around 101F. Staff indicated cheese sauce was placed into walk-in cooler when they became busy during lunch time. Discussed proper cooling practices with food employee on duty and recommended using shallow metal pans on the speed rack in the walk-in cooler. Also discussed rearranging walk-in cooler to make more room for speed rack and cooling practices. Educational handouts were left with staff. 
->Cheese sauce was portioned into shallow metal pans and placed into the walk-in cooler.
->Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature would likely not have cooled to 41°F or less within 4 hours based upon observations and information provided by staff. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed food employee transfer a raw hamburger to grill with gloved hands, then discard gloves and proceed to continue food preparation touching clean utensils and surfaces in the kitchen without a handwash in between. 

->Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Discussed importance of handwashing after handling raw animal products. Reference 2-301.14(G).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed raw shell eggs stored directly above container of ready-to-eat pickles and squeeze bottle of ketchup in the coco-cola cooler near the restrooms. Refrigerator was reorganized at the time of inspection. 

->Store raw animal products by cooking temperature and below ready-to-eat foods to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Chlorine dish machine behind the bar found sanitizing with concentrations less than 50 ppm chlorine at the time of inspection. Test strips were provided. 
->Ensure concentrations are between 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Verify proper concentrations with test strips. Reference 4-501.114.

The following food contact surfaces found soiled: 
1. interior of chlorine dish machine located behind bar soiled with scale build-up
2. piercing tip of table top can opener soiled with food debris
->Food contact surfaces of cooking/baking equipment must be cleaned and sanitized at least once ever 24 hours. Reference 4-602.12.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Spaghetti noodles 50F, fettucine noodles 45F, spiral noodles 48F found stored in lidded plastic containers in the 3 door make table cooler across from the cookline. Staff indicated items were cooked on 3/24/19 and noodle cooling process consists of chilling cooked noodles in water bath and then transferring to containers for cold holding until customer order. 

->Discussed importance of proper cooling practices and different methods to achieve proper cooling temperatures. Ensure food items reach 41F prior to portioning into lidded containers. 
->Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food items were discarded. Reference 3-501.14.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Kitchen: Sliced tomatoes 68F-70F observed sitting at room temperature at the beginning of inspection. Staff indicated items were being sliced for lunch. Tomatos transferred into shallow pan and placed into walk-in cooler for cooling. 
Walk-in cooler: Lettuce 48F-50F in lidded, deep plastic container. Staff indicated lettuce was prepped less than 1 hour to inspection. Lid was removed for more rapid cooling. 
Customer service area in the dining room: cut lettuce 45F and tomatoes 44F on ice bath for taco toppings. Noted the items not submerged in the ice, or lids to assist in temperature retention. 

->Please ensure cold holding temperatr. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
The following items found without proper date marking, located in cooler behind the bar: cocktail sauce (prepped on 3/9,discarded), gusto sauce (Staff indicated prepped 3/22, labeled on site), 1000 island (no date, discarded).

->Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.
